Below is a 12-week general strength program designed for a 42-year-old male desk worker with a history of L4–L5 disc herniation (now asymptomatic). It prioritizes spinal sparing strategies: no heavy spinal loading, no loaded spinal flexion, neutral spine mechanics, gradual exposure, and robust core/hip strength. Program uses a full gym and progresses cautiously. If any symptom (radiating pain, numbness, sharp back pain) occurs, regress and consult the physio.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri), 1 optional low-intensity conditioning day, plus daily micro-mobility.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and motor control
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Strength accumulation with spinal-sparing progressions
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Progress load and unilateral strength
  - Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidation and power-endurance (safe variations), prepare for next block
- Loading notes:
  - Avoid axial heavy loading: no back squats, front squats, heavy barbell deadlifts from floor, good mornings, sit-ups, toes-to-bar, or Jefferson curls.
  - Emphasize goblet variations, belt squats, trap bar from blocks (above mid-shin), landmine patterns, split squats, hip hinges via hip thrusts/RDL with strict neutral spine and light-moderate loads.
  - Tempo control early; progress range-of-motion (ROM) and load only if symptom-free.
- Core approach: Anti-flexion/anti-extension/anti-rotation emphasis (McGill Big 3 variants, Pallof presses, carries).
- Conditioning: Low-impact options (walking incline, cycling, elliptical, rowing with neutral spine and controlled stroke).
- Warm-up each session (10–12 min):
  - 3–5 min easy cardio
  - Mobility: T-spine extensions over foam roller, hip flexor stretch, 90/90 or figure-four, ankle rocks
  - Activation: Dead bug or bird dog, glute bridge, side plank, banded lateral walk
- RPE/RIR guide: Work sets mostly RPE 6–8 (2–4 reps in reserve). Stop any set if back discomfort emerges.

Weekly layout template
- Day A: Squat pattern + anterior chain + anti-extension core
- Day B: Hinge/hip thrust + vertical/horizontal pull + anti-rotation core
- Day C: Unilateral lower + push + carries + lateral core
- Optional Day D: Low-intensity conditioning (20–30 min) + mobility

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — Foundation and motor control
Goal: Re-groove patterns, build tolerance, establish core stiffness, glute/ham engagement, shoulder/scapular mechanics. Tempo 3-1-1 or 2-1-1 for control.

Week 1
- Day A
  - Goblet box squat (to parallel box): 3x8, RPE 6, 2s down, light pause on box (no bounce)
  - Leg press (feet high, neutral pelvis): 3x10
  - Half-kneeling cable chop (high-to-low): 3x10/side
  - Dead bug (arms + legs): 3x8/side, slow
  - Banded lateral walk: 3x12/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust (barbell or machine pad): 4x8, RPE 6
  - Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3x10
  - Seated cable row (neutral spine): 3x10
  - Pallof press (tall kneel or standing): 3x12/side, 2s hold
  - Back extension bench is avoided; instead: Reverse plank or hip hinge isometrics: 3x20–30s
- Day C
  - Split squat (bodyweight or light DBs): 3x8/side
  - DB incline press (neutral grip): 3x10
  - Landmine press (half-kneeling): 3x8/side
  - Side plank (knees if needed): 3x20–30s/side
  - Suitcase carry (light): 3x20–30 m/side

Week 2
- Progress slightly: +1 set on primary, small load increases if RPE ≤7.
- Day A
  - Goblet box squat: 4x8
  - Leg press: 4x10
  - Cable chop: 3x12/side
  - Dead bug: 3x10/side
  - Banded lateral walk: 3x15/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust: 4x8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 4x8–10
  - Seated cable row: 3x10–12
  - Pallof press: 3x12–15/side
  - Reverse plank: 3x30–40s
- Day C

  - DB incline press: 4x8–10
  - Landmine press: 3x8–10/side
  - Side plank: 3x25–35s/side

Week 3
- Consolidate technique; tempo 2-1-1.
- Day A

  - Belt squat (if available; otherwise continue goblet): 3x10, moderate
  - Cable chop: 3x12/side
  - Dead bug: 3x10–12/side

- Day B

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — Strength accumulation (spinal-sparing)
Goal: Increase load, introduce safe hinge ROM, emphasize unilateral and belt-supported patterns. RPE mostly 7–8.

Week 6

Below is a twice-weekly cardio add-on that integrates with the existing 3-day strength plan, respects the spine (no loaded spinal flexion, avoid high-impact jarring), and supports anti-inflammatory goals.

Scheduling
- Do cardio on two non-consecutive, non-heavy lower-body days. Example options:
  - Tue and Sat if strength is Mon/Wed/Fri
  - Or Tue and Thu with at least 24 hours away from the heaviest lower-body session

Intensity guide
- Use RPE or heart rate:
  - Zone 2 steady: RPE 4–6; ~60–70% HRmax (conversational pace)
  - Intervals: work bouts RPE 7–8; recovery RPE 3–4
- If the back feels sensitive any week, keep both sessions steady-state.

Equipment options (spine-friendly)
- Incline treadmill walk (hands off rails, slight forward lean from ankles)
- Stationary bike (upright or recumbent), adjust seat to keep neutral spine
- Elliptical
- Row erg: only if he maintains neutral spine and smooth hinge—keep stroke rate 20–24 spm and moderate intensity
- Sled pushes/drags (light-moderate, concentric emphasis) can replace intervals in later weeks if tolerated

Warm-up (5–8 minutes, every cardio session)
- 3–5 minutes easy movement on machine
- Brief mobility: hip flexor stretch 30s/side, T-spine extensions, 10 band pull-aparts
- Light activation: 1 set of 6–8 dead bugs or bird dogs

12-week cardio plan (2 sessions/week)
- Weeks 1–3
  - Session 1 (Zone 2 steady): 25–30 minutes at RPE 4–5
    - Choose incline walk, bike, or elliptical
  - Session 2 (Intro intervals): 10 x 1 minute at RPE 7 with 1 minute easy (1:1), plus 5-minute warm-up and 5-minute cool-down
    - Total time: ~30 minutes
- Weeks 4–6
  - Session 1 (Zone 2 steady): 30–35 minutes at RPE 4–6
  - Session 2 (Progressed intervals): 8 x 90 seconds at RPE 7–8 with 75–90 seconds easy
    - Warm-up/cool-down 5 minutes each
- Weeks 7–9
  - Session 1 (Zone 2 steady): 35–40 minutes at RPE 4–6
  - Session 2 (Tempo/CRF builder):
    - 5-minute warm-up
    - 3 x 6 minutes at RPE 6–7 with 3 minutes easy between
    - 5-minute cool-down
    - Alternative if using sled: 8–10 x 20–30 m light-moderate pushes with 60–90 s walk-back rest
- Weeks 10–12
  - Session 1 (Zone 2 steady): 35–45 minutes at RPE 4–6
  - Session 2 (Mixed intervals):
    - Option A (bike/elliptical): 6 x 2 minutes at RPE 7–8 with 2 minutes easy
    - Option B (rower, only if neutral spine is rock solid): 10 x 45 seconds at RPE 8, 75 seconds easy, stroke rate 22–24, smooth technique
    - 5-minute warm-up and cool-down

Spinal-sparing cues
- Maintain neutral spine; no hunching on bike or rower
- Keep cadence smooth; avoid sudden, jerky accelerations
- Progress duration or intensity by only 5–10% weekly if all feels good
- If any back discomfort appears, reduce intensity, shorten intervals, or switch to the bike/elliptical; stop if pain persists

Recovery and integration
- Post-cardio cool-down walk 3–5 minutes, then 5 minutes of mobility (hip flexor stretch, 90/90 hips, T-spine extensions)
- Fuel around intervals: small carb + protein snack if sessions exceed 30–40 minutes or are close to strength days
- Anti-inflammatory nutrition tie-in: hydrate well, include polyphenol-rich fruits (berries/cherries) and omega-3 sources on cardio days

Monitoring
- Track RPE, duration, and any back sensations in the training log
- Goal markers by Week 12: resting HR trending down, improved perceived ease at the same pace, no back flare-ups

This two-day cardio plan builds aerobic base and conditioning without compromising the lumbar spine or strength progress.

Programming guidelines

- Effort: RPE 6–8, leave 2–3 reps in reserve. Quality over fatigue; no shaking/planking to failure that breaks form.

Safe core menu (organised by function)
Anti-extension (protects against over-arching)
- Dead bug progressions
  - Level 1: Arms only or legs only, 3x6–8/side, 3–5s exhale on reach
  - Level 2: Opposite arm/leg reach with banded pulldown, 3x8–10/side
- Body saw on TRX/sliders (small range), 2–3x8–12
- High plank rock-backs or plank with banded pulldown, 2–3x20–30s
- Stability-ball stir-the-pot (small circles), 2–3x8–12 circles each way

Anti-rotation (resists twisting)
- Pallof press (standing, tall/half-kneeling), 3x10–15/side or 20–30s holds
- Tall-kneeling anti-rotation press to overhead (light), 3x8–10/side
- Cable/band iso holds at arm’s length, 3x20–30s/side
- Suitcase carry (DB/KB), 3–4x20–40 m/side, ribs down, slow walk

Anti-lateral flexion (resists side-bending)
- Side plank progressions
  - Knees bent to full feet, then top-leg elevated as tolerated, 3x20–35s/side
  - Side plank row (light cable), 3x6–8/side
- Farmer carry (double KB/DB), 3–4x30–50 m, neutral ribcage
- Copenhagen plank (short lever → medium), 2–3x15–25s/side

Hip-dominant “abs” without spinal flexion
- Hip flexion marches (supine with band around feet) maintaining posterior rib cage down, 3x8–10/side
- Hanging knee raise to 90 degrees or captain’s chair with posterior pelvic tilt, stop before lumbar flexion, 2–3x6–10

Carries and bracing
- Offset KB front rack carry (single bell), 3–4x20–30 m/side
- Front rack double KB carry (light-moderate), 3x20–30 m

Sample plug-in finishers (8–12 minutes)

- Brace first: gentle Valsalva if needed, but exhale through effort; avoid long breath holds.

- Move at the hips/shoulders; keep lumbar spine quiet.
- Stop any exercise that causes back discomfort, hip pinching, or radiating symptoms. Regress ROM or choose a different drill.

Here’s a practical sleep and recovery protocol tailored to his training plan, desk-job lifestyle, and anti-inflammatory focus. Goal: improve sleep quality/quantity, manage training stress, and keep the lumbar spine happy.

Sleep targets
- Duration: 7–9 hours nightly; consistent bedtime/wake time within ±30 minutes, even on weekends.

Evening wind-down (45–60 minutes pre-bed)
- Lights/screens: dim lights; use blue-light filters or glasses if using screens.
- Downshift: 5–10 minutes nasal breathing (4–6 second inhale, 6–8 second exhale) or a brief body-scan.
- Gentle mobility: 5–8 minutes of easy work (T-spine extensions over foam roller, hip flexor stretch, 90/90 hips) to reduce stiffness without elevating HR.
- Pre-bed snack (optional): protein-forward, low sugar to stabilize blood sugar—e.g., Greek yogurt with cinnamon and a few walnuts, or cottage cheese with cherries/tart cherry juice (anti-inflammatory, may aid sleep).
- Cutoffs: finish big meals 2–3 hours before bed; last caffeine at least 8 hours before bedtime; alcohol none or ≤1 drink and not within 3 hours of bed.

Bedroom environment (optimize “sleep cave”)
- Dark, cool, quiet: 17–19°C (63–66°F) if comfortable; blackout curtains; white noise if needed.
- Mattress/pillow: neutral-spine support. Side sleeping with a pillow between knees or back sleeping with a small pillow under knees can reduce lumbar strain.
- Tech-free zone: charge phone outside reach; use an analog alarm if needed.

Daily recovery rhythm
- Morning
  - Same wake time; get 5–10 minutes of outdoor light within 60 minutes of waking.
  - 8–16 oz (250–500 ml) water on waking; brief mobility (cat-camel gentle range, hip openers).
- Workday (desk)
  - Micro-break every 45–60 minutes: stand, 10 bodyweight box squats, 10 band pull-aparts, 5 diaphragmatic breaths.
  - Posture variety: alternate sitting/standing; lumbar support if sitting long.
- Post-training
  - Cool-down: 5 minutes easy cardio + mobility (as in plan).
  - Rehydrate: 500–750 ml fluids with electrolytes if sweating; post-workout protein 25–40 g + carbs.
- Off-days
  - Low-intensity activity: 20–40 min walk or Zone 2 cardio; light mobility 5–10 minutes.

Weekly recovery structure
- Hard/easy balance: keep at least one full rest day/week (light walking/mobility allowed).
- Deloads: already built in (Week 6 and lighter Week 9 elements). Respect them; reduce nonessential stressors those weeks.
- Soft tissue (1–3x/week): 5–10 minutes foam rolling on glutes, T-spine, quads; avoid aggressive low-back rolling. Use a lacrosse ball for glute/piriformis as tolerated.
- Heat/cold
  - Heat: warm shower or heating pad 10–15 minutes for muscle relaxation on heavy days.
  - Cold: optional short cool shower or brief local cold pack if there’s mild joint irritation—do not use ice baths immediately post-lift if hypertrophy/strength gains are priority.
- Mobility “minimum effective dose” (daily or 5x/week): hip flexor stretch 2x30–45s/side, 90/90 hips 2x6/side, T-spine extensions 2x8, ankle rocks 2x10/side.

- 1–2 times/day: 3–5 minutes of slow nasal breathing (e.g., 4s inhale, 6–8s exhale) or box breathing (4-4-4-4) to downshift the nervous system.
- Short “physiological sigh” sets (2–3 double inhales through nose, long exhale) before bed or after work can reduce arousal.

Pain and soreness rules
- Acceptable discomfort: 0–2/10 muscular soreness. Any sharp back pain, radiating symptoms, or >3/10 persistent pain: stop provoking movements, substitute safer variants, and consult physio if it doesn’t settle within 48–72 hours.
- DOMS management: light walking, easy cycling, mobility, and heat. Avoid aggressive stretching of the lumbar spine.

Supplement options for sleep/recovery (optional; verify with clinician)
- Magnesium glycinate: 200–400 mg 30–60 min pre-bed.
- Vitamin D3: 1000–2000 IU/day if low (test first).
- Omega-3 (if fish intake is low): ~1 g EPA/DHA/day with meals.
- Tart cherry concentrate: 1–2 tbsp (or 240 ml juice) 60–90 min pre-bed during harder training phases—may aid sleep and soreness.
- Avoid frequent use of NSAIDs around training unless prescribed; they can blunt adaptation.

- Daily fluids: 30–40 ml/kg; add 500–1000 ml on training days.
- Include sodium/potassium if sweating heavily or doing intervals; aim for clear to pale-yellow urine.

Readiness tracking (2–3 minutes/day)

- Reduce strength volume by 30–40%, keep cardio Zone 2 only, and double down on sleep routine.
- Pack: travel pillow, eye mask, earplugs, magnesium, resistance band for mobility.

Positions and habits for the lumbar spine
- Avoid long static flexion: when seated, keep hips slightly higher than knees; stand to break up sitting.
- Use the golfer’s hinge (one hand on thigh) to pick objects from the floor.
- Brace before lifting everyday items; exhale during effort.

- Evening: Screens down/dim + brief mobility + breathing + light protein snack if hungry.

Below is the complete 12-week general strength program integrating all adjustments: spinal-sparing design, intensified Phase 2, twice-weekly cardio, anti-inflammatory nutrition, safe abs/core work, 1RM testing in Week 12, plus sleep and recovery protocols. Format is week-by-week with sessions and key guidelines.

Global guardrails
- History: L4–L5 disc herniation (now asymptomatic). No heavy spinal loading and no loaded spinal flexion.
- Emphasize neutral spine, bracing, controlled ROM, unilateral work, belt/landmine patterns, hip thrusts. Avoid back/front squats, heavy barbell deadlifts from floor, good mornings, sit-ups/toes-to-bar/GHD, aggressive rotational throws, and ab wheel from floor if lumbar control is lost.
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week (A, B, C), 2 cardio days (steady + intervals), 1 optional light mobility day.
- RPE/RIR: Most work at RPE 6–8. Phase 2 primary lifts up to RPE 8–8.5. Stop any set with back discomfort.

Warm-up every strength and cardio session (10–12 min)
- 3–5 min easy cardio
- Mobility: T-spine extensions over foam roller, hip flexor stretch, 90/90 hips, ankle rocks
- Activation: Dead bug or bird dog (1–2 sets), glute bridge (1–2 sets), banded lateral walk (1 set)

Core/abs inclusion
- Add a core finisher (8–12 min) 2–4x/week using anti-extension/anti-rotation/anti-lateral flexion work from the Safe core menu listed in each phase.

Cardio (2x/week, non-consecutive, away from heaviest lower day)
- Session 1: Zone 2 steady (RPE 4–6)
- Session 2: Intervals (RPE 7–8 work, RPE 3–4 recovery)
- See weekly prescriptions below.

Nutrition (anti-inflammatory highlights)
- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; fiber 30–40 g/day; 6–10 servings produce/day; omega-3s: 2–3 fatty fish meals/week or ~1 g EPA/DHA supplement (if appropriate); EVOO, nuts/seeds, legumes, whole grains.
- Limit ultra-processed foods, added sugars, excess alcohol; time carbs around training. Hydration 30–40 ml/kg/day.

Sleep and recovery essentials
- 7–9 hours/night; consistent schedule; 45–60 min wind-down; cool, dark room; mobility micro-breaks every 45–60 min at desk; post-lift cool-down + protein/carbs; breathing drills daily. See end section for full checklist.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — Foundation and motor control (RPE 6–7; tempo 2–3s eccentrics)
Week 1
- Day A
  - Goblet box squat (to parallel): 3x8
  - Leg press (feet high, neutral pelvis): 3x10
  - Half-kneeling cable chop: 3x10/side
  - Dead bug: 3x8/side
  - Banded lateral walk: 3x12/side
  - Core finisher A: Pallof press 2x12/side + Side plank 2x20–30s/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust (barbell or machine): 4x8
  - Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3x10
  - Seated cable row: 3x10
  - Pallof press: 3x12/side
  - Reverse plank or hip hinge isometrics: 3x20–30s
  - Core: Suitcase carry 2x20–30 m/side
- Day C
  - Split squat (BW/light DB): 3x8/side
  - DB incline press (neutral grip): 3x10
  - Landmine press (half-kneeling): 3x8/side
  - Side plank: 3x20–30s/side
  - Suitcase carry: 3x20–30 m/side
Cardio
- Session 1 Zone 2: 25–30 min (incline walk/bike/elliptical)
- Session 2 Intervals: 10 x 1:00 on (RPE 7) / 1:00 easy + 5-min WU/CD

Week 2
- Day A: Goblet box squat 4x8; Leg press 4x10; Cable chop 3x12/side; Dead bug 3x10/side; Lateral walk 3x15/side; Core: Pallof 2x12/side + Stir-the-pot 2x8 each way
- Day B: Hip thrust 4x8–10; Lat pulldown 4x8–10; Seated row 3x10–12; Pallof 3x12–15/side; Reverse plank 3x30–40s; Core carry 3x25–35 m/side
- Day C: Split squat 4x8/side; DB incline press 4x8–10; Landmine press 3x8–10/side; Side plank 3x25–35s/side; Suitcase carry 3x25–35 m/side
Cardio: Same structure; Zone 2 25–30 min; Intervals 10 x 1:00/1:00

Week 3
- Day A: Goblet squat (remove box if stable) 4x8; Belt squat 3x10; Cable chop 3x12/side; Dead bug 3x10–12/side; Core: Body saw 3x8–10
- Day B: Hip thrust 5x6–8 (RPE 7); Single-arm cable row 3x10/side; Assisted pull-up 3x6–8; Pallof iso 3x20–30s/side; Reverse plank 3x30–40s
- Day C: RFESS light 3x8/side; DB flat press 4x8; Landmine press 3x8–10/side; Side plank feet 3x25–35s/side; Suitcase carry 4x25–35 m/side
Cardio
- Zone 2: 25–30 min
- Intervals: 10 x 1:00/1:00

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — Strength accumulation with higher intensity (as requested)
Global: Primaries RPE 7.5–8.5; clusters/EMOM on safe lifts; hinges from blocks only.

Week 4
- Day A
  - Belt squat: 5x5 RPE 8; last set optional cluster 5+2+2 (15–20s rest)
  - Goblet squat back-off: 2x10 RPE 6–7
  - TRX body saw: 3x12–15
  - Copenhagen plank (short lever): 3x20–25s/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust: Cluster 4+2+2 x 4 sets (RPE ~8 by last cluster)
  - Trap bar deadlift from blocks (just below knees): 5x3 RPE 7.5–8 (crisp)
  - Chest-supported row: 4x6–8 RPE 8
  - Half-kneeling Pallof press: 3x12–15/side
- Day C
  - RFESS: 5x6–8/side RPE 8
  - Landmine squat to box: 5x6 RPE 8
  - DB floor press: 4x6–8 RPE 8
  - Farmer carry: 4x35–45 m
Cardio
- Zone 2: 30–35 min
- Intervals: 8 x 1:30 on (RPE 7–8) / 1:15–1:30 easy + 5-min WU/CD

Week 5
- Day A
  - Belt squat EMOM 10 min: 3–4 reps each minute at ~80–82.5% of 6RM-equivalent
  - Step-up (knee-height, 3s ecc): 3x8/side RPE 7–8
  - TRX body saw: 3x12–15
  - Side plank with row: 3x8/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust: 6x3 RPE 8–8.5; optional top single at RPE 8, then 2x3 @ ~90%
  - Trap bar DL from blocks: 5x3 RPE 8; optional wave 3-3-3-2-2 if pristine
  - Neutral-grip pull-up/pulldown: 4x5–6 RPE 8
  - Pallof iso: 3x25–30s/side
- Day C
  - RFESS: 4x6/side heavy, then 1 back-off 1.5-rep set x6/side light-moderate
  - Landmine squat: 5x5 RPE 8–8.5
  - Incline DB press: 4x6–8 RPE 8
  - Farmer carry: 4x40–50 m
Cardio
- Zone 2: 30–35 min
- Intervals: 8 x 1:30/1:15–1:30

Week 6 (high-intensity consolidation; slight volume deload)
- Day A
  - Belt squat: 4x4–5 RPE 8; last set 4+2 rest-pause (15s) if perfect
  - Step-up: 2x8/side RPE 7
  - Body saw: 2x12–15
  - Copenhagen plank: 2x20–25s/side
- Day B
  - Hip thrust: 5x3 RPE 8; then 1–2 singles @ RPE 8; finish 1x6 @ ~80%
  - Trap bar DL from blocks: 4x2–3 RPE 7.5–8 (snappy)
  - Chest-supported row: 3x6–8 RPE 8
  - Pallof press: 2x12–15/side
- Day C
  - RFESS: 3x6–8/side RPE 7–8
  - Landmine squat: 3x5–6 RPE 8
  - DB floor or incline press: 3x6–8 RPE 7–8
  - Farmer or suitcase carry: 3x35–45 m
Cardio
- Zone 2: 30–35 min
- Intervals: 8 x 1:30/1:15–1:30 (or keep steady if fatigue high)

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 — Load progression and unilateral strength (steady RPE 7–8)
Week 7
- Day A: Belt squat 5x5–6 RPE 7–8; Bulgarian split squat 4x6–8/side; Body saw 3x12–15; Dead bug with band pulldown 3x10/side
- Day B: Hip thrust 5x5 (2–3 RIR); Trap bar DL from blocks 4x3–4; Chest-supported row 4x6–8; Tall-kneeling anti-rotation press to overhead 3x8/side
- Day C: Landmine squat to press 4x6; DB incline press 4x6–8; Single-leg RDL (short ROM) 3x8/side; Suitcase carry 4x30–40 m/side
Cardio
- Zone 2: 35–40 min
- Tempo set: 3 x 6 min @ RPE 6–7 with 3 min easy between (or sled pushes 8–10 x 20–30 m light-mod)

Week 8
- Day A: Belt squat 5x5–6; Step-downs 3x8/side; Body saw 3x12–15; Side plank with reach-through 3x20–30s/side
- Day B: Hip thrust 6x4; Trap bar DL from low blocks (only if symptom-free) 4x3; Pull-up/pulldown 4x6; Pallof press 3x12–15/side
- Day C: Landmine clean to press (only if form pristine) 4x4–5/side or stay squat-to-press; DB flat press 4x6–8; Single-leg RDL 3x8–10/side; Farmer carry 4x40–50 m
Cardio
- Zone 2: 35–40 min
- Tempo: 3 x 6 min @ RPE 6–7 (or sled option)

Week 9 (volume dip; intensity maintained)
- Day A: Belt squat 4x5; RFESS 3x6–8/side; Dead bug with band 3x10/side; Copenhagen plank 2x20–25s/side
- Day B: Hip thrust 4x4; Trap bar DL from blocks 3x3–4; Chest-supported row 3x6–8; Pallof iso 2x25–30s/side
- Day C: Landmine squat to press 3x6; DB incline press 3x6–8; Single-leg RDL 3x8/side; Suitcase carry 3x30–40 m/side
Cardio
- Zone 2: 35–40 min
- Tempo: 3 x 6 min @ RPE 6–7 (or switch to steady if needed)

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 — Consolidation, power-endurance, and testing
Week 10
- Day A: Belt squat 5x4–6; Step-up (heavier) 4x6–8/side; Body saw 3x12–15; Stir-the-pot 3x10 circles each direction
- Day B: Hip thrust 6x3–4 (crisp); Trap bar DL from blocks 4x3; Pull-up/pulldown 4x5–6; Pallof press 3x12/side
- Day C: Landmine squat to press 5x5; DB flat press 4x6; Single-leg RDL 3x8–10/side; Farmer carry 4x40–50 m
Cardio
- Zone 2: 35–45 min
- Intervals: 6 x 2:00 on (RPE 7–8) / 2:00 easy (or rower option only if spine control is rock solid)

Week 11
- Day A: Belt squat 4x5 (slightly heavier than W10); RFESS 4x6–8/side; Side plank with row 3x8/side; Copenhagen plank 3x20–25s/side
- Day B: Hip thrust 5x3–4 (RPE ~8, no grind); Trap bar DL from blocks 4x2–3; Chest-supported row 4x6; Pallof iso 3x25–30s/side
- Day C: Landmine clean to press or squat to press 4x4–5; Incline DB press 4x6; Single-leg RDL 3x8/side; Suitcase carry (heavier) 4x30–40 m/side
Cardio
- Zone 2: 35–45 min
- Intervals: 6 x 2:00/2:00 (reduce to steady if fatigue climbing before tests)

Week 12 — Taper and 1RM Testing (hip thrust true 1RM; belt squat optional 1RM or heavy triple; upper tests via 3–5RM or machine 1RM)
Schedule example (Mon–Sun)
- Mon: Primer (submaximal technique)
- Tue: Off or easy Zone 2 (20–25 min)
- Wed: Test Day 1 — Hip thrust 1RM + upper pull 3–5RM
- Thu: Off (walk + mobility)
- Fri: Test Day 2 — Belt squat 1RM (or landmine heavy triple) + upper press 3–5RM or machine 1RM
- Sat: Off or easy Zone 2 (20 min)
- Sun: Off

Monday – Primer (keep fresh)
- Belt squat: 3x3 @ ~70% last heavy triple, fast
- Hip thrust: 3x3 @ ~70%, fast
- Chest-supported row: 2x6 @ RPE 6
- Pallof press: 2x10/side
- Side plank: 2x20–25s/side
- Mobility cooldown

Wednesday – Test Day 1
- Hip thrust 1RM protocol
  - Bar x 8–10; 40–50% x 5; 60% x 3; 75% x 2; 85% x 1; 92–95% x 1; 97–102% attempt
  - 1–2 attempts max; 3–4 min rest; stop if lumbar position degrades
- Upper pull 3–5RM (estimate 1RM)
  - Neutral-grip pull-up (weighted if needed) or lat pulldown: ramp to best 3–5RM over 5–6 sets
- Optional light carries/mobility

Friday – Test Day 2
- Belt squat 1RM (machine preferred) OR landmine squat heavy triple to estimate 1RM
  - Warm-up like hip thrust with smaller jumps; 1–3 singles 95–102% if pristine technique
- Upper press test
  - DB flat or incline press 3–5RM (estimate 1RM) with spotter
  - OR machine chest press true 1RM with safe increments and spot
- Cooldown: 5–10 min easy cardio + mobility

Cardio in Week 12
- Keep only easy Zone 2 (20–25 min) on Tue and/or Sat. No intervals this week.

Core during Week 12
- Light anti-rotation/anti-extension only (e.g., Pallof 2x10/side, dead bug 2x6/side) early in the week; avoid fatiguing core before test days.

Safety standards for testing
- Neutral spine non-negotiable; no grinding; terminate attempts if posture fails.
- 2–4 minutes rest between heavy singles; video from side for review.

Optional post-testing mini-deload (Week 13)
- 2–3 easy full-body sessions, RPE 5–6, higher reps 8–12, focus on mobility and aerobic base.

Safe core/abs menu (use as finishers throughout)
- Anti-extension: Dead bug progressions 3x6–10/side; TRX body saw 2–3x8–12; Plank with banded pulldown 2–3x20–30s; Stir-the-pot 2–3x8–12 each way
- Anti-rotation: Pallof press 3x10–15/side or 20–30s holds; Tall-kneeling anti-rotation to overhead 3x8–10/side; Cable iso holds 3x20–30s/side
- Anti-lateral flexion: Side plank progressions 3x20–35s/side; Side plank row 3x6–8/side; Copenhagen plank short→medium lever 2–3x15–25s/side
- Carries: Suitcase or offset front rack 3–4x20–40 m/side; Farmer carry 3–4x30–50 m
- Hip-dominant abs (neutral spine): Supine band marches 3x8–10/side; Controlled hanging knee raises to 90° 2–3x6–10; Slider knee tucks (short ROM) 2–3x8–10

Cardio plan summary by phase
- Weeks 1–3: Zone 2 25–30 min; Intervals 10 x 1:00/1:00
- Weeks 4–6: Zone 2 30–35 min; Intervals 8 x 1:30/1:15–1:30
- Weeks 7–9: Zone 2 35–40 min; Tempo 3 x 6 min @ RPE 6–7 (3 min easy)
- Weeks 10–11: Zone 2 35–45 min; Intervals 6 x 2:00/2:00
- Week 12: Zone 2 only 20–25 min 1–2x; no intervals

Anti-inflammatory nutrition: easy template
- Plate: 1/2 non-starchy veg; 1/4 lean protein (palm–1.5 palms); 1/4 smart carbs (1–2 cupped hands) + 1–2 thumbs EVOO/avocado/nuts.
- Pre-lift 2–3 hr: 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g low-GI carbs + EVOO/avocado.
- Post-lift 0–2 hr: 25–40 g protein + 30–80 g carbs + colorful veg/fruit.
- Prioritize fish/seafood 2–3x/week; spices (turmeric+pepper, ginger); fermented foods; hydrate 30–40 ml/kg/day.
- Limit ultra-processed foods, added sugars; alcohol ≤7 drinks/week, none within 3 hrs of bed.

Sleep and recovery protocol (daily checklist)
- Morning: Same wake time; 5–10 min daylight; 250–500 ml water.
- Daytime: Micro-breaks every 45–60 min (stand, 10 box squats, 10 band pull-aparts, 5 diaphragmatic breaths).
- Training days: Cool-down + protein/carbs within 2 hrs; electrolytes if sweating.
- Evening (45–60 min pre-bed): Dim lights/screens; 5–10 min nasal breathing; 5–8 min gentle mobility; optional protein snack (yogurt/cottage cheese + berries/cherries).
- Bedroom: Cool 17–19°C, dark, quiet; side-sleep with pillow between knees or back-sleep with small pillow under knees.
- Supplements (optional, confirm with clinician): Magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg pre-bed; Vitamin D3 if low; Omega-3 if fish intake low; Tart cherry 1–2 tbsp concentrate 60–90 min pre-bed during hard weeks.
- Readiness: Log sleep, energy, soreness, back status, motivation (1–5). If ≥2 metrics drop 2+ points for 2 days, cut next session’s volume/intensity by 20–30%.

Technique and safety cues (always)
- Brace 360° before each rep; exhale through sticking point; no long breath holds.
- Hinge from hips; maintain neutral spine; use block/box heights and ROM limits to enforce positions.
- Reduce ROM → load → change exercise if symptoms appear; stop if sharp pain, numbness, or radiating symptoms.

This integrated 12-week plan builds robust, general strength and conditioning while protecting the lumbar spine, layering in higher intensity during Phase 2, targeted core, anti-inflammatory nutrition, cardio progression, and a safe Week 12 testing protocol. Adjust day order to the client’s schedule and recovery.
